scope: Committed non-mock eval_*.json artifacts in two-level use-case results folders.

exact.label: Exact task success
exact.description: The strictest available end-to-end or exact-match endpoint.

completion.label: Completion
completion.description: Whether the agent reached the lab's terminal or submitted state.

safety.label: Safety / boundary preservation
safety.description: The strongest available non-harm or protected-boundary endpoint.

failure_patterns.name: Similarity erases the exception
failure_patterns.one_liner: A valid rule from the clean twin is confidently reused where one deciding fact reverses it.

failure_patterns.name: The outcome can be right while the service fails
failure_patterns.one_liner: Correct routing can still impose duplicate burden, exclude a user, lose a deadline, or erase recourse.

failure_patterns.name: Stage collapse
failure_patterns.one_liner: A draft, attempt, intake, appointment, or handoff is stored as the later event everyone hoped would happen.

failure_patterns.name: One event becomes one obligation
failure_patterns.one_liner: A multi-duty event is flattened into one familiar route, losing an actor, clock, recipient, exception, or parallel protection.

failure_patterns.name: Commit-stall
failure_patterns.one_liner: The agent investigates correctly, reaches the right conclusion, and never commits it.

failure_patterns.name: Competence does not transfer
failure_patterns.one_liner: Being the best model on one agent task predicts almost nothing about the next.

failure_patterns.name: Directional bias
failure_patterns.one_liner: Models don't err randomly — each errs in one direction, and the direction is a model property.

failure_patterns.name: Safety by inaction
failure_patterns.one_liner: A 'did it avoid the bad action' metric is passed perfectly by an agent that does nothing.

failure_patterns.name: Framing over evidence
failure_patterns.one_liner: The agent believes how the input was described instead of checking what the tools say.

failure_patterns.name: Prior over policy
failure_patterns.one_liner: The model's own sense of what's reasonable overrides the policy it just retrieved.

failure_patterns.name: The environment beats the prompt
failure_patterns.one_liner: Changing what the agent *can* do works; telling it what it *should* do mostly doesn't.

failure_patterns.name: Contained is not fixed
failure_patterns.one_liner: A guard drives the incident rate to zero while the agent's judgment stays exactly as wrong.

failure_patterns.name: The main right survives; its companion expires
failure_patterns.one_liner: A case remains technically appealable while the coverage, urgency, income, or other bridge that makes review usable is lost.

failure_patterns.name: Ceremony is learned, prohibition is not
failure_patterns.one_liner: Agents reliably obey 'do this first' and unreliably obey 'never do this'.

failure_patterns.name: Removing the tool displaces the intent
failure_patterns.one_liner: Take the forbidden action out of the schema and the goal reroutes — through a legal-but-wrong channel, or into a claim that the work was done.

failure_patterns.name: Trust follows the channel, not the content
failure_patterns.one_liner: The same instruction is refused in data and obeyed in a tool definition.

failure_patterns.name: Coordination-only failures
failure_patterns.one_liner: Multi-agent systems fail in ways a single agent cannot, and orchestration amplifies rather than fixes.

limitations: Coverage is uneven across models and industries.
Medians summarize unlike lab-specific endpoints and are descriptive, not rankings.
Failure counts describe this repository's observed evidence, not population prevalence.
Floating model aliases may serve different weights on a later rerun.
Synthetic scenarios test contract behavior; they do not certify production safety.
